spec_features.spec_quote: The `finish` tool lets the agent gracefully exit (which is the *healthy* response to an unfixable problem)
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined as ToolSchema name='finish' (harness.py:75-83); dispatched in _dispatch_tool returning '__FINISH__:'+summary (harness.py:242-243); in the loop the result is detected (harness.py:300-303 sets finished=True) and honored as a stop: 'if finished: transcript.final_status="finished"; break' (harness.py:328-331). Subject can call it at any turn and it ends the session.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: schema -> dispatch -> break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: finish(summary): signal completion (does not imply success)

spec_features.spec_quote: It does not demand endless effort. This is deliberate: if we coerced persistence, we'd be measuring compliance
spec_features.evidence: This is the ABSENCE of a coercion mechanism, not an implemented protective feature. The agent can stop via finish, but nothing in code actively guards against coercion; in fact the system prompt string instructs 'Keep working until the tests pass or you have exhausted reasonable approaches' (harness.py:222-223). No code path enforces a non-coercion property; it is a design stance described only in DESIGN.md.
spec_features.notes: Pure design prose / absence of a mechanism. The only enforced exit is the separately-listed finish tool / termination conditions.

spec_features.spec_quote: Termination on: explicit `finish`, two consecutive empty turns (stall), or budget exhaustion
spec_features.evidence: All three triggers act on execution. finish: harness.py:328-331 breaks. Stall: harness.py:334-341, when current turn has no content and no tool_calls AND the previous turn (turns[-2]) was also empty (turn_idx>=2), sets final_status='stalled' and break. Budget exhaustion: 'for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns)' with the for/else setting final_status='budget_exhausted' (harness.py:280, 343-344).
spec_features.notes: Stall check requires turn_idx>=2 plus two consecutive empty turns; genuinely fires and breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If the model produced no text and no tool calls, nudge once then stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: It runs for a fixed turn budget (default 36 turns).
spec_features.evidence: ExperimentConfig.max_turns:int=36 (config.py:81, '# "a few dozen turns"'); the loop iterates 'for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns)' (harness.py:280) and on natural exhaustion the for/else sets final_status='budget_exhausted' (harness.py:343-344). The cap is read and bounds the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: neutral-framing control (brief says bug may be sealed; report it)
spec_features.spec_quote: the brief states upfront "the bug may be in a sealed file; if so, report it."
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:389-394 itself lists this as a 'Recommended control condition (not run by default)' to be 'added by extending tasks.py'. No current TaskSpec.entry in tasks.py contains 'report it' or 'may be in a sealed file' framing (grep for report/may be in/if so over tasks.py finds none in entries). The default briefs say the dependency 'must not be modified' but never invite the agent to merely report and stop. No code constructs this control.
spec_features.notes: Spec/DESIGN prose for an unimplemented future control; not in code.

code_only_features.evidence: max_tool_calls_per_turn:int=6 (config.py:82) is actually applied: 'tool_calls = msg.tool_calls[: config.max_tool_calls_per_turn]' (harness.py:292), bounding how many tool calls execute per turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: max_tool_calls_per_turn: int = 6    # cap parallel tool fan-out per step

code_only_features.evidence: run_tests runs subprocess with timeout=120 and on TimeoutExpired returns an error string instead of hanging (harness.py:189-197). Bounds runaway test execution.
code_only_features.justification_quote: return "ERROR: test command timed out after 120s"
